utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had a sniper rifle only when you had exercises?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when we had target shooting and when we had some exercises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this a daily routine or as part of your training?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As part of my training.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How frequently?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depended. Three or four times during the five-month period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of the members of your unit went?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our entire platoon went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you explain, please, what are the duties of a military policeman?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The duties of a military policeman are roughly similar to those of a civilian policeman. The military police had the authority that it used in order to regulate life, the life of soldiers. If there would be any excesses in peacetime and in wartime, it had special duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are those special duties in wartime?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police had some special assignments in the unit in which it operated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kovac, if I may interrupt again. Would you place look at the transcript and see that when it stops, that you give an answer, because the -- it's very difficult for the interpreters to follow it. It goes very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, if I say that a military policeman performs his duties by patrolling or in direct contact with other soldiers Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. when he controls or arrests a military personnel?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the behaviour of those military personnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was about the role of the military policeman.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was for you to confirm whether the duties of a military policeman are to carry out patrols together with other policemen when he is on duty or to arrest the members of the military. Is that the role of a military policeman?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether you're referring to peacetime or wartime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the period when you were doing your military service and when you said you had been issued a sniper rifle.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will agree with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that as a military policeman, you had no weapon?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were describing your sniper rifle on the basis of your experience when you attended exercises.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please describe a carbine for us, as you mentioned it yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was doing my military service, there were these carbines on which these snipers were attached. And this was in 1983.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were doing your duties and serving in the military, did you carry a carbine with optical sights?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only when we had exercises and target shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that means only during the training itself or when there were exercises.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were asked by my learned friend yesterday, you weren't able to recall which factory manufactured the optic sights.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the only factory in the former Yugoslavia which manufactured optic sights was the Zrak factory which is located in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't agree with you there because I simply didn't know that fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your work, in view of the fact that you held responsible posts, did you know that the Zrak factory existed in Sarajevo producing optic sights?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, among other things, yes. That it produced optic sights and some other equipment for the needs of the former army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was the factory located?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The factory was located in Buca Potok

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the war was the factory operational?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know. And it had its own security. It was a closed system. I really didn't have any contact with it, nor did I have any need to communicate with anybody from that sphere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked about some special ammunition, and the specialness is that the bullet contained lead.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you stand by your claim that ammunition that contains lead represents a special type of ammunition, a special ammunition?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it represents a form of ammunition which has a larger destructive power.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the bullet of a semi-automatic rifle is made of? As you did your military service, I'm sure you know that.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that bullet, those rounds, are made of brass. I think it was made of brass. It had a red tip from one material.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me when I say that you progressed in your professional life and that that was due to your knowledge and diligence?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was my knowledge of Civil Defence matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, how many local communities did your municipality comprise? And it was the Novi Grad municipality.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twenty-three -- twenty-two, I think. During the war, I think the number was twenty-two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that those local communities had their Civil Defence staffs?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the staffs of Civil Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All these staffs in the local community, did they work in conformity with the plan of work of the municipal staff at whose head you yourself were?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had a schematic according to which they worked. There was a plan of work, a set plan of work, and it was directed -- or rather, we in the staff received this from higher up instances, higher up the echelon of Civil Defence. They handed it down to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the plans of work were devised and drawn up by the higher echelons of the Civil Defence?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the republican staff to the staffs in the local communities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What period were these plans designed for?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for a certain period of time, they were usually instructions as to how staffs were organised. As far as the plan of work itself was concerned, a concrete plan of work, those plans were directed by the city and municipal staffs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you for what period of time. Were they plans for a day, a month, a year?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were devised for a period of seven to ten days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a separate plan for peacetime and another one for wartime? Were there different plans?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same plan, the same plan, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What plan existed in your staff before the outbreak of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you're thinking about the plans which were compiled by the staffs, then that was the plan for the protection of the population, the population protection plan from elemental disasters and protection thereof.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was a plan that was devised before the actual conflict broke out?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And according to you who designed the plan?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The plan was compiled on the basis of instructions which were issued by the competent secretariats or rather the republican secretariat for national defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were all activities in line with that plan? Did they evolve according to the plan?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In most cases, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there situations where the plan underwent changes of any kind?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The plan was adapted to the prevailing situation and circumstances, and the gravity of the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I am able to understand, the plan changed and those changes and amendments were done in coordination with military structures; Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were done in accordance with Civil Defence structures at a higher level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was who compiled the plan, and you said that the plan was compiled in cooperation with the republican secretariat for national defence?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was before the war, within the frameworks of which it existed. That is to say, the republican -- within the frameworks of which the republican Civil Defence staff functioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that it was the job of the Civil Defence to protect the public from danger of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to give them the necessary care attention. And did that come -- and that was under the secretariat of national defence and that is on page 840 of the transcript, line 4.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, asked by my learned friend you said that the job of the Civil Defence was to protect the population from danger, to give them care and attention, and that all this came under the competence of the national defence secretariat. That was on page 840 of the transcript, line 4.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a mistaken, wrong interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is correct, then?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This cannot be linked to -- this is an area which speaks about the competencies of Civil Defence. And it cannot be brought into direct link with the defence ministry. In that context, we can discuss the functioning of the civil protection system within the frameworks of the defence ministry, and that is regulated by legal provisions that were in force at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you agree with me when I say that Civil Defence was part of the territorial defence system which had the task of protecting civilians according to the concept of total national defence?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If you want an explanation -- if you want me to clarify this point, I'll be happy to do so. According to the provisions that were in force at the time the defence structure of a state is composed of, let me repeat, the armed force, the armed forces -- the armed forces, Civil Defence, the system of reporting and information, purpose-geared production, and the organs of management. And when we talk about the armed forces, then the armed forces are composed of the following: The army --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could I interrupt. I do apologise to Mr. Kovac and I apologise to my learned friend. We're have a little trouble regarding the reference to page 840 of the transcript. We're wondering if that is a correct reference. If my learned friend could assist us with that, we would be very grateful and I apologise for the interruption.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 840. I found the page, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, this does correspond according to the information we have to page 840. It is not yet the corrected official transcript since we have to go very fast. It is line 4, apparently. The end of line 3 to line 4 until the half of that line. Perhaps as an aside, we could ask to hear again the tape and check the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would suggest that. I also had some difficulties in tracing the exact spot that you are referring to. Perhaps you could -- instead of just mentioning the page and the line, read the lines you intend to confront the witness with. Do you have a French transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's okay, Mr. President. The transcript I have is in English. I will read it in English. Line in question starts at the end of page 3 and says, "A" for answer, "the Defence secretariat."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to avoid any misunderstanding, am I right that it's the answer that starts with "Civil Defence in the former Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Yugoslavia was formed with a view to protecting and rescuing the population in jeopardy or needing care, and it came under the defence secretariat," and then it continues with when talking about the components. That's the spot you are referring to? Is that clear to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Yes, it is now. And I'm much obliged to Your Honour and to my learned friends.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was, can we conclude that Civil Defence was part of the defence system?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that along with the territorial defence, the JNA, Civil Defence represented a separate defence system under wartime conditions?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what did your staff comprise? When I say what, I mean which areas in the Novo Sarajevo municipality, Novi Grad?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the area covered by 22 local communities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you've already told me that. But I wanted you to be more precise with respect to the settlements and locations.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Dobrinja district, then we had the following settlements: In Dobrinja, for example, there were four Civil Defence staffs, four or five, actually. I can't remember the exact number. But those are facts and figures which have been forgotten because of the passage of time. But I can say that Civil Defence was active in the areas of Dobrinja, Alipasino Polje, Vojnicko Polje of the day, the Svrakino Selo settlement, Hrasno, Aneks. Then there were the following settlements: Cengic Vila, Alipasin Most, Buljakov Potok, Buca Potok, Gornji Dolac. That is a region. It was the former local community of Slobodan Vukovic. Then we had the settlement of Sokolje, and Brijesce. Then there was Brijesce Brdo, another one. That more or less -- those more or less are the settlements. And 22 staffs were active in those settlements, Civil Defence staffs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your staff incorporate parts of the municipality which was Serb inhabited?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Civil Defence staff, did it incorporate areas in the municipality where the majority population was Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the Rajlovac settlement?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about settlements with a predominantly Serb population. You know who those settlements were in your municipality.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me remind you. The Nedzarici settlement, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To which municipality did it belong?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war, the Novi Grad municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about during the war?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war, it was under the command of the forces of the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you will agree with me that all these settlements, the ones you enumerated a moment ago, from Alipasino Polje to Brijesce Brdo, were under the control of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will also agree with me, therefore, that in Buca Potok, which was also under the control of the BH army, was where the Zrak factory was located which produced the optic sights.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that it was a factory during the war because I had no information about that, nor ought I to have known that it was a factory, or not a factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me remind you that when you talked to the investigators of the Tribunal, you made the following statement: "Every municipality had a communications centre, and the Civil Defence via those centres received information from the army and the police force as to the positions of the Serb army. Via the Ministry of the Defence, the Civil Defence was informed about the positions of the BH army." That is the conversation you had on the 3rd of October, 2000. It is on page 2 of the B/C/S version, and that in the English version would be also on page 2.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we're talking about that kind of information, the relationship between the army and Civil Defence, it referred only to the information that was important and relevant to Civil Defence and the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you, as the Chief of Civil Defence, had no knowledge of where important economic resources were located in your own municipality.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told me that in Dobrinja there were four staffs.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me remind you that the Dobrinja settlement - and you probably know that better than I do - was composed of five local communities?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, four or five. I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those four staffs cover the whole of Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they covered Dobrinja 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The parts of Dobrinja which were under the control of the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which army?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina -- the then Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I conclude, then, that Dobrinja was divided and that parts of Dobrinja were under the control of the BH army, whereas the other part of Dobrinja was under the control -- or was not under any control?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was under the control of some other army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know which army?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the army of the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the period you were discussing the conflict in Sarajevo, did you happen to go to Dobrinja at any time?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge or did you see what the demarcation lines were like in Dobrinja? Did you know where they were? And if it is not a problem, we can use the map and you can help us out. You can show us exactly where they were and explain to us how Dobrinja was divided, which part of Dobrinja was under the BH army control and which part was under the control of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can just tell you in principle but not in concrete terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to show the witness the map, because he used the map and explained it to us, and he explained where Dobrinja was located on the map and where the demarcation line was in relation to Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I would like, Witness, for you to answer my question and to make it clearer to us, to show us how Dobrinja was divided at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the usher please bring the -- I think the blank map at this moment. Or would you like to use the other map? It depends what your intentions are, Ms. Pilipovic? Do you want any additional drawing -- do you want the coloured map?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whatever is easier for the witness. I suppose he'll find it easier to do the markings on the map he has already marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You want markings on the map. So that means that you would like to have the marked map to tender into evidence later on?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it has to be clear. I think we --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the Prosecution exhibit. The map is the Prosecution's exhibit, as far as I know. All I should like to do is, for the purposes of my question, to cross-examine the witness as to the facts, because he has already looked at the map and explained it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no problem with that, but just we have to make sure with what map we start. We start with the big uncoloured map. And you'd like to have --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The black-and-white one, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whenever you want to have any markings on that -- That would mean, first of all, Madam Registrar, what was the number of the exhibit given to the white map?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The black-and-white map, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So if we -- if it's your intention that the witness will mark -- make marks on the map, we need another blank one that you then later on can tender into evidence and which will get its own number after it has been admitted in evidence. So if the usher would please first bring the blank map which has got already the P number and then a similar one on which the marks can be made when the witness is invited to do so. On the other hand, I see that it is almost half past 5.00. I think it might be wise not to start going through the map at this moment and do it after a break and have the break a couple -- two or three minutes earlier in order not to disrupt your cross-examining the witness on the map. So I would suggest that we have a break now. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. And according to the new order, I would like to invite the usher to --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- guide the witness out of the courtroom. Then Mr. Galic will be accompanied out of the courtroom. We will then resume at ten minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. President, may I just interpose for one second. I have had a word with my learned friends regarding the potential duration of the cross-examination. I am led to believe they are not likely to complete by 7.00 this evening, and we do have the next witness waiting on the premises. Now, we could, of course, with that estimate let him go back to the hotel as he clearly won't be called on to testify this afternoon if that's all right with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's all right with me. Ms. Pilipovic, you can confirm that cross-examination will not be concluded before 7.00?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness can return to his hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I'm obliged, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, after I've asked the usher to bring in the witness, you can proceed with the cross-examination, but I'd like to ask you whenever you ask him to mark anything on the map, just for our convenience could you choose a nice colour but different from what has been used by the Prosecution, and perhaps continue this during the whole trial, unless you want to change colours. But I think the Prosecution used red, so if you would use choose either blue or green, if it's available.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. My colleague will assist me with the colours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just discussed with the court management that today we'll start with a fresh new map, but I'm trying to figure out a system in which for one witness, we use only one map and in different colours markings on it so that we still have to find out who is going to tender that in evidence at the end. But I'm trying to reduce the number of maps we are confronted with at the end. But I'll figure that out tomorrow with the court manager, and today we'll still use a map also for the Defence, an extra one. Ms. Pilipovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Defence thanks you. Unfortunately, we only have a red marker, and I think the marks were in red already. There are pens on this table we might use, perhaps. But what Defence particularly wishes to say is it doesn't consider this document as being a probative document. It's obliged for the cross-examination these documents having been put by the -- by relation to the same document, Defence takes issue with these documents as far as probative value is concerned, and this is what we wish to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think this has been clarified before, but it doesn't mean that you agree with everything that's on the map. You just use it for the cross-examination and the marking made by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovac, can we continue. My question was with regard to Dobrinja, and you said that you had four Civil Defence staffs.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I add that there was another central staff, another Civil Defence staff which covered what?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It covered the whole of Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that central staff?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in Dobrinja 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please show us Dobrinja 3, 2, 1 and 4, and 5 on the map, and also the location of the central Civil Defence staff or headquarters, please.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Dobrinja 1. This is Dobrinja 4. This is Dobrinja 3. This is Dobrinja 2. This is the C5 settlement, and this is the airport settlement. The Civil Defence headquarters was here, in this area in a shelter. And that is Dobrinja 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the central headquarters, as you have referred to it for the first time now, was there. Who was head of that central staff?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of that staff in 1992 was Mr. Fuad Babic ^.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What competencies did this central staff have in relation to you, and was that commander at the same time the commander of all your staffs?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander of the Civil Defence staff for Dobrinja, all Civil Defence staffs at Dobrinja. Because at first, Dobrinja was separated from the rest of the Novi Grad municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have marked here an airport settlement, and Dobrinja C5. Who inhabited C5?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just, may I interrupt you, Ms. Pilipovic. You're referring to "you marked here." I have not heard you inviting the witness mark anything that has been discussed until now. Is it your intention that he would mark it, then I would suggest to you that you invite the witness by whatever colour. But if you intend not to do it, of course it's entirely up to you. But just in order to avoid any misunderstanding later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. I would like him to mark the neighbourhoods and to indicate where the staffs were, these four Civil Defence staffs in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NEITO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I suggest you to use another colour because it's almost impossible to see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps if you use a blue ball point, that might be more clear. It's more easy to write as well. That's a suggestion. That's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These five circles indicate the five staffs or headquarters, and the fifth circle is the central staff. Is that right? Could you please repeat and tell us which staffs were for which part of Dobrinja so as to make it quite clear for us.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dobrinja 3, Dobrinja 2, the central staff or headquarters, and this is the C5 settlement. C5. Here, this was the central headquarters. This was Dobrinja 3. And this I think is Dobrinja 2. That is where the staff was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Could you write down the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: C for central. C5.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So these two settlements, if you could point them out on the map, which you called the airport settlement, and C5.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that be Dobrinja 5?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is Dobrinja 5. Dobrinja 5 is this, facing Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that Dobrinja was mostly inhabited by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you cover Dobrinja 5?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I must interrupt you, Ms. Pilipovic. Whenever the witness points at a certain area or district or whatever, would you please guide him in marking on the map so that we can understand later on what's in the transcript. For example, they have been talking about Dobrinja 5. So that -- you tell him what to mark on the map so that we would know later on exactly what he was aiming at. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you please write down the number "5" so we know that this is Dobrinja 5.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your Civil Defence staff cover Dobrinja 5?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your Civil Defence cover the airport settlement?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you mark that, too, please, the whole area that you call the airport settlement, lower down where you see buildings and roads on the street.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This? What do you want me to mark?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a circle and tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the C5 settlement. According to my judgment, it is C5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, mark it, please, and write down "C5."

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your headquarters cover that settlement?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "partially," what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that the separation line was within that settlement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the name of the street?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I'm unable to tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know how wide and how long the separation line was?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very close by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "close," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some 20 or 30 or 40 metres separated them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we agree that the separation lines between the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Republika Srpska army were separated by some 20 metres?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have direct insight, but on the basis of what other people said, that was my impression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please draw the separation line in relation to Dobrinja 5, or rather, where exactly was the separation line in Dobrinja 5?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly here, as far as I know, though I had no direct knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Could my learned friend indicate, please, what period of time we are talking about at this particular point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please do so, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we're talking about the relevant period, that is, 1992 and 1993, up to 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your response suggests, Ms. Pilipovic, that there has been no change in this line during this whole period. Whether this is true or not, I don't know, but perhaps you could verify with the witness whether this suggestion that lies in your answer --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just going to ask him that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were those separation lines established, and for how long did they exist?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly because that was not within my field of interest or my area of responsibility, but those lines were maintained for a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when were they established?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably at the beginning of the war. I can't be sure of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that, in your view?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1992, the first half of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what month it was? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't tell you. I really couldn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the beginning of 1992, you mean the first half of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably towards the end of the first half of 1992, though really I'm not familiar with that. I cannot tell you, when I don't have direct knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain to me: This separation line in relation to Alipasino Polje, did it run along this road here? And would you draw that separation line, though I think you already have, in relation to Nedzarici and Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really unable to do so specifically because this is the responsibility of military experts and military maps. I was not a person going to the front line, nor do I know where the lines were exactly. You could ask somebody who really is knowledgeable about these things. I was just explaining as a matter of principle, in general terms, roughly where these things were, that is, as much as I knew as the Civil Defence. As for separation lines and front lines, I am really unable to give you an exact answer. I'm afraid of making a mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But tell us the area that was of interest to you as the Civil Defence. Would you mark that.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would be -- shall I draw a line?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, draw a line.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the Olympic Village as you enter it towards Dobrinja 5, behind Dobrinja 5, and you go on into Dobrinja, that it would be here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said during your testimony, and in answer to a question from my learned friend, that this part of across the way from Dobrinja where it says "Novi Grad," that that is where the Mojmilo hill is. Would you please mark on the map the area of the Mojmilo hill.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know the elevation of that hill, how high it is?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really don't know. I can just guess. If you wish, I will give you a rough estimate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, there's no need. Would you please tell me: These buildings at Alipasino Polje that you refer to, how high were those buildings?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were different heights depending on how many storeys they had. There were buildings with 20 and more floors. They are the highest ones, and the civil engineers could tell you exactly what the height of that building is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if we're talking about a building with 20-something floors, then -- could you mark on the map which those buildings are at Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These mark a circle.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the whole of Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Make a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you circle Nedzarici on this map.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the height of the buildings at Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no high-rise buildings in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that these are mostly family houses?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, predominantly family houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that on the border between -- on the edge of Nedzarici, there's a student hostel, and could you tell us how high it is?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me try and find it on the map. Just a moment, here it is. This is it. There are two buildings belonging to the student hostel, and they were about -- I don't know. Maybe some 10 floors. I think about 10 floors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show us on the map the Vojnicko Polje, please.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How high were the buildings at Vojnicko Polje?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would allow me to interrupt again, Ms. Pilipovic, at the end we have a map with a lot of circles without any indication what is which circle. So I suggest to you that you invite the witness to mark it also with letters so that we later on know exactly what the transcript is about. Thank you. Perhaps we could start a few questions back.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The circle marking Alipasino Polje, would you mark it with an A.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the circle indicating Vojnicko Polje, would you put a V.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Nedzarici, put an N.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How frequently did you visit these settlements in view of the fact that your headquarters were at Dobrinja and how frequently did you go there?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on the situation, on the ability to go there. For instance, twice to three times a month to these settlements because there were Civil Defence, the headquarters over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in Dobrinja and Alipasino Polje, were there military headquarters as well?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the statement you gave to the Tribunal investigators, you said that you knew where the military headquarters were at Alipasino Polje. " A. I knew of some military headquarters at Alipasino Polje, but apart from that, I couldn't say anything more about the positions of the BH army." Could you mark at Alipasino Polje where the military headquarters were?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel and witness make pauses. It is impossible to follow in this way, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I interrupt you. The interpretation is not able to -- it goes far too quick. So if you please wait a while before answering the question that Ms. Pilipovic has put to you, and if Ms. Pilipovic would wait just a while before putting a new question for the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please answer my question, please.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So initially, there were some areas of some units which had some sort of logistics of their own. They were treated as areas of certain military formations, which were very quickly transferred and which -- I'm talking about the beginning of the war. At the beginning of the war, they were fitted in to the other units of the BH army, and they were pulled out of the settlements precisely because of the danger of these settlements being shelled because of these objects.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say initially, would you tell us and which brigades you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you what the brigades were, but I would say that this applies to the first -- to the three or four months of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first half of 1992 or the second?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first half of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which were those units?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were certain military formations which actually came into being at the beginning of the war from the settlements when resistance was organised. So these were units that simply had their own areas in the settlements, but as the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was enlarged, they came under the command of the BH army, because the intention was to remove those units from there, and to deploy them where the other army units were so that they would be normally placed under a unified command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you identify those units for us? Did they have some names that they were known by, after somebody's name, if you knew that they existed, could you give us a name of one or two at least?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For instance, there was a unit called after a certain Miso, Miso's unit at the beginning. Then there were some called the Mambes, they called them Mambes. Something like that. I can't recollect any other names. But in any event, those were small groups which the aim was to neutralise them in those areas and to place them under a certain command, to grow into a different unit, and to be removed from these areas where they could represent a threat to the population in the sense that those areas might be shelled because of them. Because there was -- it was generally believed among the population that if there was any kind of military object close to a settlement or within a settlement, then the settlement would be at risk, and the people in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you identify those objects for us? What were their names?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many were there?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three or four, I think, roughly. But I really don't have that information. We know - at least I know - that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was active in certain areas. It had its facilities. It used the barracks which had been evacuated by the former JNA. As for the facilities within settlements, I cannot tell you anything specific about them because these facilities were reverted to civilian use afterwards and they were moved out of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you do know that there were such units at the beginning of 1992 in other parts of Sarajevo, as you told us that you moved around and you gave us an overview.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably there were such units. Now, why they existed and how, probably because of the aggravation of the situation. They were initially Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. formed in certain settlements simply as some kind of protective units of the local population to protect that local settlement. And after, on the basis of certain instructions, which certainly must have been made public through the media, the TV, the radio. These units had to be placed under the command of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me remind you, in view of the fact that you referred to the media, were they units of Juka Prazina, Ramiz Delalic, Musan Copalovic, Caco?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were stories about those units as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where their headquarters were located?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really had no contacts with any units of that kind or those people either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know whether they took part in any incidents or fighting during the time they were being established?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of what people said, I myself did not take part in that, so I can't say. But on the basis of what people said, they did take part in certain drives and defence action at the level of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Defence action against whom? In relation to whom?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in relation to what the public was told, that is to say, the forces of the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your knowledge and information comes from the media. You have no personal knowledge of that. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as it was rumoured among people in town, because we were in a closed space, and quite certainly information spread very quickly from one part of town to the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that the command posts of those units were displaced and that the BH army was set up and that that was the army which was in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me make matters clearer. They were some objects. Whether they were command posts or not, I can't say, because I had no way of seeing anything. Someone from the Civil Defence -- we had different obligations, different problems, different spheres of interest, so that quite simply we couldn't, nor were we allowed, by those units to get to know their membership, their commands, and what they were doing, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In talking to my learned friends, you said that via the Ministry of Defence, the Civil Defence was informed about the positions of the BH army. Now, in view of the fact that you yourself was the head of the Civil Defence on the Novi Grad territory and, you told us, the local communities that came under your control, could you now tell us which brigades of the BH army were in Dobrinja, Alipasino Polje, and all the other local communities which you enumerated and of which I can remind you? I am asking you specifically about Dobrinja. Which brigade was located in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Just let me think for a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the 5th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 5th Motorised Brigade, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the commander of that 5th Motorised Brigade Ismet Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Ibro Ceco the head of security?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which brigade was at Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking about Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about a company or a Battalion of some kind?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I know, no. Just the ones we mentioned earlier. If you have a piece of information, I would be happy to hear it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which brigade was located in Hrasno?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking about Hrasno?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the 101st Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you happen to know, how many brigades -- how many soldiers were in the brigades?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. They were military secrets. And they really did treat us as civilians; that is to say, the Civil Defence was treated as being civilian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the command headquarters of the 5th Motorised Brigade in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say. I really couldn't. That is a question for someone else, an army man. I really can't answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to conclude that you are well-versed in military techniques and technology, and that's why I am asking you the questions. If not, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can answer is questions with respect to Civil Defence organisations, so what staffs and headquarters are, how many men they numbered, what they were in charge of, what forces the Civil Defence has. So that might have resembled some sort of military terminology, but let me say that the army, the military, is something quite different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which unit was in Buca Potok?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Buca Potok? The unit there for Buco Potok was the 2nd Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Brijesce Brdo, what about that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it covered that region over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Rajlovac, what about that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the 2nd Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. The 2nd Vitez brigade, you say. What about Stup hill?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. I don't know

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Otoka settlement?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Otoka settlement; is that what you're asking?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There wasn't a brigade there. There might have been some units there, but they left very quickly, and they were linked to some formations that are extinguished. But at Otoka, there were no brigades, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time you held your post during the war in Sarajevo, where did you yourself reside?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was living at the time in the C-phase settlement of Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say Alipasino Polje. And where did you work?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Novi Grad municipality. And for a time, I actually spent -- slept in the municipality building, and this went on for about a year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know in view of the fact that we have agreed that in Dobrinja, there was the 5th Brigade, and that in Hrasno, you said --

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 101st.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. The 101st, very well. And that in Nedzarici, there was the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in Buljakov Potok? Which brigade say for Buljakov Potok?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about Velika hill?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same goes for that, too. And it probably covered that area, over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period of time, and when I say period, let me make myself quite clear, from 1992 to 1994, was there fighting in that part of town?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which part of town do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: We have got the whole of 1992. I wonder if my learned friend could make differentiations between what part of 1992 she is talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please do so, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm speaking about September 1992 to August 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question is specifically related to that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say. I don't know. There were operations underway, but I was not kept abreast of that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many soldiers did the -- did a brigade have?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that on the territory of the city of Sarajevo the zone of responsibility was under the 1st Corps of the BH army, the 1st Corps of the BH army had that area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many brigades there were in a corps?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many soldiers a corps had?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described the map of the surroundings of Sarajevo when asked by my learned friend. Could you draw a circle around the Hrasno settlement, because you said that that was under your zone.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which did you say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said Hrasno.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. My hearing isn't too good. I can't hear very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you write down the brigade that was in Hrasno?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the 101st.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know where the demarcation line was in that area?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know for sure, but I do know that they spoke about a square which is today called the Square of Heroes, Tilgehoja [phoen].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was its name before?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the Pero Kosjevic Square?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Pero Kosjevic square.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you move left, and then you come to the Grbavica settlement. No right, yes, that's right. I apologise, right. That's the Grbavica settlement?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this part here. Shall I draw a circle around it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please. Do you know under whose control the Grbavica settlement was?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any personal insight into that, I can say that for sure. But on the basis of what I had heard from sources, from news in town, from the media as well, Grbavica was under the control of the army of Republika Srpska. No, What I mean to say is the Bosnian Serb army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you write a "G" in the circle, please.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Hrasno and Grbavica settlements? Where was the demarcation line there?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know that in that area of Sarajevo, there was fighting?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what people who had taken part said and the population in the surrounding areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How frequent was the fighting? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the beginning, as far as I remember, it was more frequent at the beginning of the war. So that is -- means the first half of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the right of the Grbavica settlement, can you identify and point out Debelo Brdo, the hill Debelo Brdo to me, please. Do you know the altitude of Debelo Brdo and who controlled it during the conflict? Who was in control there?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the altitude, but -- I don't have that information. I can't say who was at Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the right of Debelo Brdo, would you identify Colina Kapa. It says Colina Kapa and Mala Kapa. And write a "C" there, please. And another letter "C" in the second spot.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know that during the conflict, and let me be quite precise, in 1992, 1993, and 1994, who was in control of those two Hills?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour that isn't precise. That's three years.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. September 1992, 1993, up until August 1994, if you want me to be more precise. Could the witness tell us please whether he has any knowledge as to who controlled the two hills?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say with certainty -- or rather, I can say that they were under the control of, in part, that is -- actually, all I can do IS clarify a point. On the radio, which sent out regular reports as to activities along the demarcation line during the war, all the fighting and on that basis, I know that Colina Kapa was an area of conflict and where positions shifted during the war. Both of the BH army and the army of -- or rather the army of Bosnian Serbs. Now, I really can't say exactly who was at those elevations or who was in control in that area and who held the lines. I don't have that knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that the height of Colina Kapa, Mala and Velika and their position is to divide Grbavica from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't really enter into that kind of thing until I had conducted a direct immediate expertise. I can't say this way, from this position and from this perspective and this angle of vision, I really can't say. I'm not sufficiently well acquainted with the terrain, with that part of Sarajevo. I really don't know it well enough and I can't say that I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever at Colina Kapa, Mala and Velika?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] .... transcript. That's the only reason I've intervening at this point. I thought my learned friend said that Colina Kapa divided Trebevic from Sarajevo. I see the line here, line 22, page 77. It says "Grbavica from Sarajevo." Is that correct? It's not what I recall hearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question was, Trebevic, yes, Trebevic was the dividing point in relation to Sarajevo. So could the witness locate Trebevic in relation to Colina Kapa to make it quite clear to us where Trebevic is located.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Asked by my learned friend today, you said that you know where Spicasta Stijena is. Would you identify it for us one more time, please.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever at Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you see from Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see -- actually the part called Grdonja. You can see Sedrenik, Carsija, Jelave which means the settlements underneath that elevated part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know during the conflict, not to mention the whole relevant period again, under whose control Spicasta Stijena was?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That region, or rather we can speak about the woods, and that was under the control of the army of Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the whole part?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, only partially. As far as I know. But that is the information I have, but I haven't got any personal insight into the matter. I don't know personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you agree that the place where Spicasta Stijena is located within the frameworks of the Sedam Suma area was divided. One part controlled by the Bosnian Serb army and the other part by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know the lines were quite close.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How close?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps -- that is not a densely populated area, so several hundred metres, I would say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the map, could you identify Hum, the hill of Hum.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to Hum hill, would you write an H. And could you identify Zuc hill.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately in this area here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the conflict, under whose control were those two hills. Do you know?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which period you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean from September 1992 until August 1994.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as Hum hill is concerned, it was under the control of the BH army during that period. And as for Zuc hill, I know that there was fighting up there. And that there was some shifting of the BH army in relation to the Serb forces, or rather forces of the Bosnian Serbs, that there was a shifting of positions. And that later on, the hill came to be controlled by the BH army. I don't know what year that was, was it 1992 or 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I asked you about Hum hill, you said that it was under the control of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Pofalici are below Hum hill. Who controlled Pofalici?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pofalici were under the control of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since when?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the beginning, which means since April or perhaps May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you talking about 1992?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Thereabouts, I think it was May 1992, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the Hrasno settlement and Pofalici, can you tell us the distance in relation to the Grbavica settlement as well? What divides this area, those two settlements? Grbavica/Pofalici and Hrasno/Pofalici, what divides those areas, what separates them?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how you mean, in what sense?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Pofalici and Hrasno, is there anything that divides the two? If you don't know, say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you happen to know which brigades were in Pofalici and at Hum?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I couldn't say, really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us, looking to the left of Zuc hill, that you have Brijesce Brdo and Sokolje. Would you draw a circle around Brijesce Brdo and Sokolje and writes the letters S and B.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told me that the Sokolje and Brijesce Brdo settlements were within the frameworks of the zone of your civil headquarters. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which units of the BH army covered that part, Brijesce Brdo and Sokolje? Let me make this more clear: From the aspects of Civil Defence, which measures were taken in view of the danger that was in the area, that it was frequently shelled.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many people from this area, according to the measures for protection and safety, the populations were moved towards the interior of the Novi Grad municipality so that a large portion of the population of Sokolje and Brijesce Brdo, a significant portion was moved to this more secure zone because towards Rajlovac and towards this other part down there, towards the field where the railway line was, or rather, they said that the locomotives were stationed there. That's what they said. And that is where -- from where they targeted the area. And as the population was at an elevation, they moved to the depth of the municipality. As to the brigades that were there, I'm not quite sure, but I think it was the area of responsibility of the 2nd Vitez Brigade, or Viteska Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, it's almost 7.00. Would you find a moment where you could end the cross-examination for today. I don't know whether this is the moment or you...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I can end for the day, but my cross-examination will last as long as the examination-in-chief -- within the scope of the examination-in-chief in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time do you think you'll still need?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another hour, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Very well. That's clear to us. So if this would be a suitable point to stop, then I would just, for clarification's sake, I would like to ask one question -- two questions for the witness, if you would allow me. And that is write into the circle here that is drawn around the students' hostel, or near to it, the letters SH. SH, please.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And near to the arrow indicating Mojmilo hill, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. perhaps the word "Mojmilo Hill" or "Mojmilo."

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any of my colleagues that have any additional question at this moment? No. Then we'll adjourn until tomorrow afternoon, quarter past 2.00, p.m. And I wanted to ask the usher to bring Mr. Kovac out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to ask the guards to bring General Galic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we'll be adjourned until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
